Remote Rendering Client/Server Architecture separates the volume rendering engine into a server and a client connected via a network, allowing rendering computation to be performed on a remote machine while the user interacts locally [S1][S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that a Remote Rendering Client/Server Architecture separates the volume rendering engine into a server and a client connected via a network, allowing rendering computation on a remote machine while the user interacts locally. Source [S1] explicitly describes an architecture that 'strictly separates... to individual objects... Extension of this architecture to remote rendering is therefore straightforward. The engine should be just divided in server and client parts... The server receives commands sent over the network from the client... Results of the calls can be serialised and sent back over the network to the client.' It further notes that 'the client part... should provide exactly the same application programming interface as the local version' and that 'after receiving the results, these are deserialised and used as if all the computing was done locally.' This directly supports the claim's description of separating the engine, connecting via a network, performing computation remotely, and local interaction. Sources [S2] and [S3] provide additional context on distributed rendering architectures where clients interact with remote servers for rendering, reinforcing the general concept described in the claim.
